lesson.title: Case clinic: persuasion, eligibility and prediction
lesson.summary: Compare manipulation, exploitation, social scoring and criminal prediction using changed facts.

prerequisites.reason: The case clinic includes the manipulation causal chain.
The case clinic includes vulnerability exploitation and harm.
The case clinic includes the social-scoring consequence conditions.
The case clinic contrasts unsupported prediction with fact-based human assessment.

blocks: The **harmful-decision case** follows fictional Northbridge across three proposals: a persuasive sales assistant, a service eligibility score and an individual offending predictor.
The same AI model can appear in all three, but the legal tests differ. Record techniques, vulnerabilities, evaluation over time, treatment, prediction basis and people affected.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(a)–(d), Article 6; Annex III 5(b), 6

blocks: For sales persuasion, check whether the relevant technique appreciably impairs informed choice, materially changes behaviour/decision and causes or is reasonably likely to cause significant harm. Vulnerability exploitation has its own stated basis and chain.
A helpful, accessible explanation and a deceptive harmful pressure technique have different stipulated facts. Do not classify them identically just because both influence decisions.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(a)–(d), Article 6; Annex III 5(b), 6

blocks: For eligibility scoring, test evaluation over time and the unrelated-context or unjustified/disproportionate-treatment branch. For offending prediction, test sole profiling/personality basis and the linked-facts human-support boundary.
A creditworthiness function is not automatically prohibited social scoring. A final human approver is not automatically sufficient for the criminal-risk support boundary.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(a)–(d), Article 6; Annex III 5(b), 6

blocks: The case result should cite the exact point, elements, evidence and unresolved facts. If this particular prohibition is not established, continue high-risk, scope, date and other-law analysis.
If a prohibition is established, a warning label or high-risk checklist does not cure it. The exercise teaches traceable legal reasoning rather than a permanent label for a model or vendor.

options.reason: The statutory elements need separate facts.
